def: User story: the unit of work or requirement in agile trackers (Jira, Azure DevOps, GitLab…). The course keeps the Spanish abbreviation HU.
Show, with evidence and traceability, that a user story has been tested. The sign-off is human.
A gap between the product and what was expected or contracted. You report it; you don't hide it.
Re-testing what already exists to make sure nothing broke.
A test that sometimes passes and sometimes fails without any code change (selector/timing).
The one agreed way the team writes features and steps.
Given/When/Then language for describing behavior.
Framework that wires Gherkin to code (steps).
Code that implements each Given/When/Then step.
Checking that a service honors its contract (API schema).
Page Object Model: wraps one screen's selectors and actions in a class.
Test management: links requirements, cases and runs. Examples: Xray, Zephyr, TestRail, qTest. Every company uses its own; the concept is the same.
Reports with browsable evidence; single-file = easy to attach.
The chain of links user story ↔ test ↔ run ↔ code.
The “director” AI: reasons with context, plans, keeps the method on track.
The “executor” AI: writes code right next to the repo, in the IDE.
Instructions the AI always loads in a project.
A reusable prompt template for a recurring task.
An AI agent launched for a subtask (broad search, independent perspective).
Model Context Protocol: lets the AI talk to external tools (Jira, email).
An automatic action fired by an event. In AI assistants, a hook that exits with code 2 blocks the action: that's where the non-negotiable rules live.
Tag that excludes a known issue from the run without masking the contract.
The link between an automated scenario and its case in the test management system. The mechanism (tag, ID, annotation) depends on the tool.
A pending gap owned by a third party or dependency; the ticket stays Open and doesn't close the user story.
Getting involved in design and quality early, not at the end.
Prioritizing tests by risk = likelihood × impact.
A copy of the system with exactly one thing broken on purpose, to see whether the tests notice.
KILLED: the tests caught the mutant. SURVIVED: they missed it (a real bug or a blind spot).
The unmutated run. It must pass first and doesn't count toward the score.
KILLED / (KILLED + SURVIVED). Measures how sharp the suite is, not how good the software is.
A log of survivors, discrepancies and false positives, with cause, owner and next step.
“Test the tester, mutate reality”: break the world on purpose to measure whether the guardian (suite, oracle, judge, hook) notices.
A ✓ that should have been a ✗: the answer looks right but is wrong.
A model that grades answers against a rubric or a reference, with a threshold written down beforehand.
Reference cases labeled by people using a rubric; the judge is measured against them.
Agreement between two raters corrected for chance: 1 is perfect agreement, 0 is what chance alone would give.
Cases the tuning never saw; that's where you report the honest number.
Hypotheses and thresholds committed before the data is generated.
A short code that summarizes a run's verdicts; if it matches on another machine, the verdicts match.
The number a command ends with: 0 is success and anything else is failure. It's the minimum evidence a CI understands.
Running only the tests a change can affect, with the full suite as a safety net.
A check the protected branch requires to be green before allowing a merge. Without it, a red check blocks nothing.
A file the pipeline uploads so it outlives the runner: reports, logs, hashes. The cache, by contrast, can disappear.
An environment born for one task that dies when it ends: whatever you didn't export as an artifact or receipt is lost.
A checkpoint you can resume from without repeating or duplicating work, verified by hash.
Content identifier of an image (@sha256:…). Unlike a tag, it always points to the same image.
When in doubt, or when a tool fails, do the conservative thing: run everything or mark unknown.
